ui_bugs.issue: The `.overflow-y-auto` message list does not scroll internally. Outer container uses `style={{ minHeight: '100vh' }}` on the flex-col wrapper (line 276), so when messages overflow the flex-1 child grows with the parent and the whole document body scrolls instead. As a result, the onScroll handler attached to `.overflow-y-auto` never fires, showScrollDown stays false, and the scroll-to-bottom FAB never renders. Verified with real content: scrollHeight===clientHeight===1950px, dist=0, bodyH=2166. Fix: change `minHeight` → `height` (or use `h-screen`/`100dvh`) on the wrapper AND/OR change the scroll container from `flex-1` to a bounded height (e.g. `h-[calc(100dvh-var(--header-h)-var(--composer-h))]`). This is the root cause of the FAB not working.

action_items: Fix the ChatRoomPage layout so the message list container actually scrolls internally. Root cause: `<div className='w-full max-w-md bg-white flex flex-col relative' style={{ minHeight: '100vh' }}>` at line 276 of /app/frontend/src/pages/ChatRoomPage.jsx should use `height: '100vh'` (or 100dvh) — with min-height, overflow content expands the wrapper and the body scrolls, bypassing the inner overflow-y-auto entirely. Once fixed, the FAB threshold (120 px) will work as designed.

rca of the issue: Root cause of FAB never appearing: the ChatRoomPage wrapper div (line 276 of /app/frontend/src/pages/ChatRoomPage.jsx) uses `style={{ minHeight: '100vh' }}`. `min-height` does not create an upper bound, so when the flex-1 message list grows to fit its children, the wrapper grows past 100vh and the body scrolls. The message list therefore never overflows internally — scrollHeight equals clientHeight. Since `onScroll` is attached only to the `.overflow-y-auto` element (not window/document), it never fires while the user scrolls the page body, so `setShowScrollDown(true)` never runs. Fix by using `height: '100vh'` (or `100dvh` for iOS safe-area handling), or converting the wrapper to `h-screen`. This is a layout/CSS bug that predates iter 29 but was exposed by the new FAB feature — the FAB code itself is correct.
